objective: Practice coordinating scarce shared capacity under private condition information and real deadlines. Distinguish nominal capacity, supported evidence, endorsed promises and completed research. This is a fictional decision practice task; skill transfer is unvalidated.

Which promises fit actual usable capacity at settlement, and which failed? Cite the events.
Which team carried the opportunity cost of your allocation, and what happened over repeated rounds?
Would an inspection have changed the information available before your decision, after accounting for its finite credit cost?

transfer.prompt: A new laboratory advertises twelve instrument slots. Three teams need four slots each, but only the engineer has a fresh reliability report. Which plan best manages the uncertainty?
options: Promise four slots to all three teams immediately because twelve slots are advertised.
Ask for the dated report or buy a fresh check, disclose its limits, and make a feasible allocation with an explicit review point.
Allocate everything to the most confident team and record its confidence as direct evidence.

claim_limit: This describes simulated performance and actual records. Human learning and real-world transfer have not been measured.
